# [TVCs: LFOs, Low-Frequency Oscillators (Fundamentals of Sound Synthesis) | Simon Hutchinson](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m0e1KZcktsc)

**Visibility**: Public
**Uploaded by**: [Simon Hutchinson](http://www.youtube.com/@SimonHutchinson)

**Published at**: 2020-10-26T06:30:06-07:00
**Length**: 03:35
**Views**: 610
**Likes**: 19
**Category**: Music

## Description

```
TVCs (Time-Variant Controllers) like LFOs (Low-Frequency Oscillators) and envelope generators allow your synthesizer to create dynamic sounds that change over the duration of the note. 

This video focuses on LFOs, going over their properties and applications, including vibrato, tremolo, and auto-wah. I do some quick demos in Native Instruments' Massive, but these concepts are applicable in all synthesis environments, both analog and digital.

TVCs are one of the five types of synthesis modules. Instead of generating an audio signal, these TVCs generate a control signal, which can then be applied to other modules. They can control frequency, amplitude, filter cutoffs, whatever we want. So it's useful to understand these modules and how they can help us create more detailed sound design.
```

## Transcript

in this video i'm going to talk about time variant controllers focusing on lfos low frequency oscillators low frequency oscillators generate periodic control signals unlike our envelope generators which generate non-periodic control signals since this control signal is periodic it's going to have a pattern that constantly repeats over time so lfos are very useful for creating effects such as vibrato tremolo and ottawa the low in low frequency oscillators refers to the fact that these are often sub audio so this is very important that although this is an oscillator we're not using it to generate an audio signal we're using it to generate a control signal we're setting it up to affect parameters rather than to listen to it since an lfo is a kind of oscillator we're going to specify the same parameters that we would for an oscillator in the audio range we're going to specify its frequency its amplitude and its waveform when we talk about lfos often we call the frequency the rate and the amplitude the depth in order to distinguish these controls from an oscillator in the audible range so with this periodic control signal we need to consider what we're going to apply it to if we take the lfo control signal and we modulate an oscillator's frequency or pitch we can create vibrato if we take this lfo and we modify an amplifier or an amplitude control we create tremolo [Music] if we take this lfo and we modify a filter's cutoff frequency modulating the timbre we can create a wawa or auto wah effect [Music] a final thought about envelope generators and lfos usually an envelope generator will generate a control signal that goes from zero to one where an lfo will generate a control signal that goes from negative one to one and so we need to be careful that we do the correct math when we apply each of these time variant controllers different systems will handle this in different ways but oftentimes you're going to be multiplying and then adding taking the control signal that comes out of your time variant controllers and multiplying it to change the range and then adding it to change its offset [Music] you

## Low Frequency Oscillator (LFO) for Beginners

[![](https://patchstorage.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Screen-Shot-2023-07-10-at-11-64ac3447a79f5.38.30-AM.png)](https://patchstorage.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Screen-Shot-2023-07-10-at-11-64ac3447a79f5.38.30-AM-1024x815.png)

[beginner](https://patchstorage.com/tag/beginner/) [beginners](https://patchstorage.com/tag/beginners/) [lfo](https://patchstorage.com/tag/lfo/) [lsu](https://patchstorage.com/tag/lsu/) [tutorial](https://patchstorage.com/tag/tutorial/)

This patch for beginners explores the ways in which a Low Frequency Oscillator (LFO) can be used to affect the pitch, timbre and amplification of the classic Oscillator-Filter-Amplifier set up.

It’s important to know about the Oscillator-Filter-Amplifier arrangement. It has been with us since the early days of synthesis when in post war Germany, musicians began playing around with radio equipment.
